input.description: 查 Claude 前台转后台
input.prompt:
Investigate Claude Code (installed CLI `claude`, v2.1.302 on macOS) background sessions. Time limit: 10 minutes; write partial findings to the report as you go.

Context: we build `agents`, a Rust TUI dashboard (repo /Users/example-user/Code/.worktrees/example.com/agents, read-only for you). It lists Claude sessions; live background jobs are attached via `claude attach <job-id>` (see agents/src/providers/claude/mod.rs `launch`, agents/src/model.rs `is_live_background`, agents/src/providers/claude/attach.rs). We plan to embed a session's terminal in a panel. For a plain foreground interactive Claude session (a normal `claude` process running in some other terminal), we want to first convert it into a background job, then `claude attach` it, so the panel can detach freely.

Answer with evidence (command output, help text, docs text quoted verbatim, files under ~/.claude such as jobs/ or session registries). Never quote a WebSearch/WebFetch summary as fact; quote raw text. Mark anything unverified as "not checked".
1. Is there a supported way to turn an already-running foreground interactive session into a background job? From inside (slash command, keybinding like /bg) and, importantly, from OUTSIDE the process (CLI subcommand, signal, IPC, registry file). Check `claude --help`, `claude <sub> --help` for every subcommand, the binary's strings if needed, official docs (code.claude.com / docs.anthropic.com).
2. If only from inside: could a program inject it (e.g. we already drive sessions over a pty with keystrokes)? We do NOT own the foreground process's pty, so say whether any outside route exists.
3. What happens to the original terminal when a session goes to background: message shown, does the process exit, does it auto-attach to the job, can it keep typing?
4. Alternative: `claude --resume <id>` of a session that is live elsewhere — what happens (two writers to one transcript)? Does `claude attach` work for non-background sessions? Is there a `claude --bg --resume <id>` style way to start a background job from an existing session id, and what happens to the still-running foreground process then?
5. How `agents` currently detects a live foreground Claude session (registry status idle/busy) — point to the file it reads.
Do not run anything that kills or modifies the user's existing sessions/jobs. You may start your own throwaway session in a temp dir (e.g. under /Users/example-user/.claude/jobs/594feebb/tmp/claude-probe) to test, and clean up only what you started.

Write the full report to /Users/example-user/.claude/jobs/594feebb/tmp/claude-bg-report.md and reply with the path plus a 5-line summary.
